clue.text: Fact US lawyer presented to corporation

parts.note: a DA is a district attorney, an American prosecutor
corporation is an old jocular word for a pot belly, a tum

explanation.surface: An American attorney hands a piece of evidence to a company.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Corporation' looks like a company but is the old humorous word for a paunch, giving TUM.
explanation.definitionFit: A datum is a single given piece of information, so it is a synonym for a fact.

clue.text: Liberal party at first beats a depressing situation

indicators.note: says the party word comes first, ahead of the Liberal abbreviation

parts.note: a do is an informal word for a party
drums are beaten, and to drum is to beat

explanation.surface: A Liberal party gathering, early on, is overcome by a gloomy mood.
explanation.definitionFit: Being in the doldrums is an idiom for a state of gloom or stagnation, a depressing situation.

clue.text: Inclination to take care of encyclopaedia

parts.note: to tend is to look after
ency. is a dictionary abbreviation of encyclopaedia

explanation.surface: Someone feels inclined to look after a reference book.
explanation.definitionFit: A tendency is a leaning or propensity, which is what an inclination is.

clue.text: Electronic accessory in fashion, with millions in support

indicators.note: in a down entry a supporting piece sits underneath, so the millions letter goes below

parts.note: a mode is a fashion or style
M is the abbreviation for million(s)

explanation.surface: A trendy gadget, backed by millions of pounds.
explanation.definitionFit: A modem is a device attached to a computer for connecting to networks, an electronic add-on.

clue.text: Was hazy with fourth idea for marsh

parts.note: when your head swam, it was hazy or dizzy
after plan A, B and C comes plan D, the fourth idea

explanation.surface: Someone's thinking grew foggy while they came up with a fourth notion about a bog.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Was hazy' is read as SWAM, as in a swimming head; the tempting anagram of 'Was' leaves the M unclued.
explanation.definitionFit: Swampland is wet boggy ground, a synonym for marsh.

clue.text: Plus-fours, used oddly, may possibly be unnecessary

indicators.note: possibly signals the letters may be rearranged into another word
take the odd-numbered letters, first and third, of the word used

explanation.surface: Baggy golfing trousers, worn strangely, might be surplus to requirements.
explanation.walkthrough: 'oddly' gives UE from used; 'possibly' rearranges PLUSFOURS with UE. Plus-fours are baggy knee-length trousers once worn for golf.
explanation.definitionFit: Superfluous describes something beyond what is needed, so it is a synonym of unnecessary.

clue.text: Ready to get rid of cold remnants of fire

indicators.note: says the cold letter is thrown out of the money word

parts.note: the ready is British slang for cash
C is the abbreviation for cold, as on taps

explanation.surface: Someone is prepared to clear out the cold leftovers in the grate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ready' is not the adjective but the British slang noun for money.
explanation.definitionFit: Ash is the powdery residue left when something burns, what remains of a fire.

clue.text: Change involving you and the French leads to ill-humour

indicators.note: the coins word surrounds the French words placed within it

parts.note: small change means coins, pence
French tu is you and la is the

explanation.surface: A shake-up affecting you and the French brings bad temper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Change' looks like a verb but is loose coins, PENCE; 'French' applies to both 'you' and 'the'.
explanation.definitionFit: Petulance is sulky peevishness, a form of bad temper.

clue.text: Man expressing Cockney view of beer and wine

indicators.note: a Cockney speaker drops the initial H, so the beer word loses its first letter

parts.note: a half is half a pint of beer
red is red wine

explanation.surface: A fellow giving a London East Ender's opinion on ale and claret.
explanation.walkthrough: Cockney speech, from London's East End, drops the H, so 'half' becomes 'alf.
explanation.definitionFit: Alfred is a male first name, and crosswords use Man to mean any man's name.

clue.text: Thin stringed instrument requiring two players?

parts.note: di- is the prefix meaning two, so a lute for two players is a di-lute
a lute is a plucked stringed instrument

explanation.surface: A slender lute that needs a pair of musicians to play it.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the invented word: di- (two) plus LUTE.
explanation.definitionFit: To dilute is to water down or weaken, which is to thin a liquid.

clue.text: Position taken by Irish politicians in a row

parts.note: a line is a stance taken on an issue, as in the party line
the DUP is the Democratic Unionist Party of Northern Ireland

explanation.surface: The stance adopted by Ulster politicians in a dispute.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in a row' suggests a quarrel but means in a line.
explanation.definitionFit: Things lined up stand in a straight line, one after another, which is being in a row.

clue.text: Unpleasant covering distribution of fuel

parts.note: a hat is a head covering

indicators.note: the letters of the word fuel are spread around into a new order

explanation.surface: Something nasty is concealing how fuel is shared out.
explanation.definitionFit: Hateful means arousing dislike, a stronger synonym for unpleasant.

clue.text: Symptom of cold has that man tucking into booze

indicators.note: the pronoun goes inside the spirit word, as if eating into it

parts.note: rum is a spirit, a type of booze
he is the pronoun for that man

explanation.surface: A man with a chill knocking back the drink.
explanation.definitionFit: Rheum is the watery discharge from the nose and eyes that comes with a head cold.

clue.text: Recovering soldiers not talking about island

parts.note: RE is the Royal Engineers, a British Army corps

indicators.note: the quiet word wraps around the island letter

parts.note: silent means not speaking

explanation.surface: Troops on the mend refuse to speak about an island.
explanation.definitionFit: Resilient describes bouncing back quickly from setbacks, so it fits recovering in the sense of rallying.

clue.text: Emulates tit, flying a distance

indicators.note: flying suggests the letters are sent in all directions and land in a new order

explanation.surface: Someone copies a small bird as it travels some way through the air.
explanation.definitionFit: The statute mile, 1,760 yards, is the legal land mile, a unit of distance.

clue.text: Rude mechanical i.e. an actor

indicators.note: rude here means rough or unrefined, signalling a crude reshaping of the letters

explanation.surface: A boorish workman, that is, a performer.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface recalls Shakespeare's 'rude mechanicals', the amateur players in A Midsummer Night's Dream.
explanation.definitionFit: Michael Caine is a famous English film star, an example of an actor.

clue.text: Composer right to interrupt novelist — this stuff stinks

indicators.note: the composer and right letter break into the middle of the novelist's name

parts.note: Kingsley or Martin Amis, British novelists
Alban Berg was an Austrian composer

explanation.surface: A composer barges in on a writer, and someone complains of a bad smell.
explanation.definitionFit: Ambergris is a waxy whale secretion used in perfume, notoriously foul-smelling when fresh.

clue.text: Report of wet weather costly for Lapland herd

indicators.note: a report is something heard, so the words are taken by their sound

parts.note: rain is wet weather and dear means costly

explanation.surface: A forecast of expensive rain for herders in northern Finland.
explanation.definitionFit: Reindeer are herded by the Sami people of Lapland, so a Lapland herd is made up of them.

clue.text: Expert's latitude in my operation picked up at hospital

definitions.note: read as expert is, the 's being the verb

indicators.note: in a down entry picking up raises the letters, so they read from the bottom
the latitude letter sits within the my-and-operation pair

explanation.surface: A specialist's leeway with my surgery is collected at the hospital.
explanation.walkthrough: 'picked up' turns MYLOP into POLYM; then AT and H follow.
explanation.definitionFit: A polymath is a person of wide learning across many fields, a kind of expert.

clue.text: The coldest spot in the A-Z?

definitions.text: The coldest spot in the A-Z?

parts.words: The coldest spot in the A-Z?
parts.note: the lowest possible temperature, imagined as a point that runs from A to Z, the full scale

explanation.surface: Where to find the chilliest place in a street atlas.
explanation.walkthrough: An A-Z is a London street map; A and Z are also abbreviations for absolute and zero, so the map's name hides the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Absolute zero, minus 273.15 degrees Celsius, is the coldest temperature theoretically possible.

clue.text: A slave upset husband again

indicators.note: in a down entry upset turns the word upside down, reading it from the bottom

parts.note: a serf was a bonded labourer, close to a slave

explanation.surface: A servant is distressed by her husband once more.
explanation.definitionFit: Afresh means anew or once more, a synonym of again.

clue.text: Objection over misguided King dismissing a servant

indicators.note: in a down entry the objection word sits above the rest

parts.note: but is an objection, as in no ifs or buts

indicators.note: the king sends away the letter a

parts.note: Shakespeare's King Lear is famously misguided in dividing his kingdom

explanation.surface: A protest about a foolish monarch who sacks one of his staff.
explanation.definitionFit: A butler is the chief manservant of a household, so an example of a servant.

clue.text: Fairy creature returned around course, working to provide light

indicators.note: the reversed fairy word goes around the rest
the fairy word is turned back to front

parts.note: an elf is a small fairy creature

indicators.note: working suggests the letters are worked over into a new order

explanation.surface: A sprite came back to go round the golf links, busy giving off a glow.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returned' flips the elf; 'working' scrambles course; 'around' puts the scrambled letters inside the flipped elf. 'course' looks like a golf course but is anagram fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: To fluoresce is to emit light after absorbing radiation, so to give out light.

clue.text: It's dropped when a new idea comes to mind

definitions.text: It's dropped when a new idea comes to mind

parts.words: It's dropped when a new idea comes to mind
parts.note: from the British idiom about a coin finally falling when someone at last understands something

explanation.surface: Something falls at the moment of sudden understanding.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The penny dropped' is a British idiom for finally understanding something.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom says the coin drops when realisation arrives, so it is what is dropped at a moment of insight.

clue.text: Fruit tree father's taken in hand

indicators.note: the father word is held within the hand word

parts.note: a paw is a jocular word for a hand
father is pa, the 's being is

explanation.surface: Dad holds a fruit-bearing tree in his hand.
explanation.definitionFit: The papaw is a tropical tree, also called papaya, bearing large edible fruit.

clue.text: Spain and Holland debate cutting university supplement

parts.note: E is the international vehicle code for Spain
NL is the code for the Netherlands, often called Holland

indicators.note: the university letter is cut out of the debate word

parts.note: to argue is to debate

explanation.surface: Two European nations hold talks that cut back on a university's extra funding.
explanation.definitionFit: To enlarge is to add to or augment, so it is a synonym of the verb supplement.

clue.text: Eastern game revealing self-confidence

parts.note: go is the Japanese board game

explanation.surface: An Oriental board game shows how sure of yourself you are.
explanation.walkthrough: Go is an East Asian board game played with black and white stones, which suits the Eastern surface.
explanation.definitionFit: Ego is a person's sense of self-esteem, close to self-confidence.

clue.text: Elaboration of prime South Australian motto

indicators.note: elaborating the word prime works its letters up into a new arrangement

parts.note: SA is the abbreviation for South Australia

explanation.surface: An Adelaide resident's leading slogan, worked up in more detail.
explanation.definitionFit: An impresa is a heraldic device with an accompanying motto, so the word also denotes the motto itself.

clue.text: House adjourned, about to receive indication of the future?

indicators.note: the adjourned word goes around the receive word

parts.note: Parliament rose when it adjourned
to cop is slang for to get or receive, as in cop a fine

explanation.surface: Parliament has risen and is on the verge of getting a sign of what is coming.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' looks like 'on the point of', but it is the container signal. 'House' is abbreviated Ho., and Parliament is said to rise when it adjourns.
explanation.definitionFit: A horoscope is an astrological forecast, a claimed sign of what lies ahead; the question mark flags doubt.

clue.text: Anger after disposing of one, receiving zero value

indicators.note: the shortened anger word takes in the zero letter
the anger word has thrown out the letter for one

parts.note: wrath is fierce anger
a means one
O looks like zero

explanation.surface: Once fury is shed, nothing comes in, so what is it worth?
explanation.definitionFit: Worth is the merit or monetary amount of something, a synonym of value.
